cards.text: Ezra, a priest and scribe (Ezra 7:11), is telling this one himself. He and the exiles have made it to Jerusalem, handed over the silver and gold for God's house, and offered burnt offerings (Ezra 8:32-35). Then the leaders come to him with that "got a minute?" look, and NOBODY who says "got a minute?" only needs a minute.
The leaders' report is about the surrounding peoples. They say those peoples have abominations like those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians and more.

cards.question: The leaders say the people of Israel haven't done something with those surrounding peoples. What haven't they done?

cards.text: The leaders say this reaches all the way to the priests and Levites. They also say the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land.

cards.question: The leaders say the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. How did that happen?

answers.text: They married women from those peoples
They traded in those peoples' markets
They served in those peoples' armies

cards.question: The leaders' report says the leaders and officials stayed out of this unfaithfulness.

cards.text: When Ezra hears this report, it hits him HARD.

cards.question: When Ezra hears the leaders' report, he tears his tunic and cloak.

cards.text: Ezra pulls out some hair from his head and beard, and he sits down in horror.

cards.question: Because of the exiles' unfaithfulness, people start gathering around Ezra as he sits in horror. Who gathers around him?

answers.text: Everyone who trembled at God's words

cards.text: Ezra sits there in horror until the evening offering. Then he gets up, his tunic and cloak still torn.

cards.question: At the evening offering, Ezra gets up with his tunic and cloak still torn. What does he do next?

answers.text: Kneels and spreads his hands to God
Writes a letter to the king

cards.text: On his knees, Ezra tells the LORD he's ashamed and embarrassed to even lift his face to Him.

cards.question: Ezra prays that their iniquities are higher than their heads and their guilt has reached the heavens. He's saying their guilt is ___.

cards.text: Ezra says their guilt has been great from the days of their fathers to this day. He says they and their kings and priests were handed over to the kings of the earth, and it's still that way this day.

cards.question: Ezra names the sword, captivity, pillage and humiliation. Why does he say all that came on them?

answers.text: Because their walls were too weak
Because their kings made no treaties

cards.text: But then Ezra's prayer turns. He says that for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD their God to preserve a remnant and give them a stake in His holy place.

cards.question: Even in their bondage, what does Ezra say God has given the people?

answers.text: New life and light to their eyes
Herds and flocks in every field
Grain and wine in their storehouses

cards.text: Ezra says it straight: they're still slaves, but their God has not forsaken them in their bondage. Friend, back in my junk drawer, I'd have FRAMED a line like that and hung it right over the takeout menus.

cards.question: Ezra says God has extended grace to His people in the sight of which kings?
Ezra says God's grace gives them new life to ___ the house of their God and repair its ruins.

cards.text: On top of that, God's given them a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
Then Ezra says, "And now, our God, what can we say after this?"

Ezra says they have forsaken the commandments God gave through His servants the prophets. Those commandments called the land they were entering polluted by the impurity of its peoples, filled with abominations from end to end.

cards.question: The commandments Ezra quotes say not to give their ___ in marriage to the sons of those peoples.
The commandments Ezra quotes tell Israel to seek the peace and prosperity of those peoples.
In the commandment Ezra quotes, why are the Israelites told to stay apart from those peoples?

answers.text: So they could be strong and pass the land on
So they could pay less to foreign kings
So they could rule over every nation

cards.text: Ezra looks back at everything that's come on them because of their evil deeds and their great guilt. And he admits something about how God has handled it.

cards.question: Ezra says God has punished them more than their iniquities deserve.

cards.text: God even left them a remnant like this one. So Ezra asks, shall they AGAIN break His commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations?

cards.question: If the people break God's commandments again, what does Ezra ask whether God would do?

answers.text: Wipe them out with no survivor
Send them back down to Egypt
Give their land over to Moab

cards.text: Then Ezra comes to his last words, and friend, there's not ONE "well, technically" anywhere in them. He calls out to the LORD, God of Israel.

cards.question: As Ezra ends his prayer, what does he say the LORD, God of Israel, is?
Ezra says that because of their guilt, no one can stand before God.

cards.text: Here they are before God in their guilt, still a remnant this day. Hold that thought, friend, because this batch is still in the oven.
